subject: Control/Data handoff: deployment artifact inventory & ephemeral routing plan
messages:
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lin Wu <lin.wu@brytecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for the ACME private deploy - artifacts we need

Hi Soojin / Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. For the cutover window on 10/12 we want to make sure we have a minimal, reviewable artifact set for our infra team to validate routing and egress constraints.

Can you: 
- Share a single CSV index of files we should expect from Redwoods (diagrams, manifests, runbooks)
- Confirm the control-plane endpoints we will need to allow in our firewall rules (IPs/FQDNs)
- Call out any ephemeral egress requirements (NAT ranges, STUN/TURN, or third-party telemetry endpoints)

Lin from BryteCloud is copied for any crossconnect questions. If you can get the index and a short egress policy by EOD Monday that would let us schedule the rack-level test.

Thanks,
Jake
Senior Infra Lead, Acme Corp

Attachment: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Lin Wu <lin.wu@brytecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data handoff: deployment artifact inventory & ephemeral routing plan

Hi Jake —

Attached is a compact index (vpc_artifact_index.csv) that enumerates what we will deliver for the ACME pilot. Summary below for quick consumption: 

Key artifacts you will receive:
- controlplane-diagram-v2.drawio.png — logical control-plane endpoints, ports, and authenticated paths
- ephemeral-egress-policy.yaml — suggested NAT ranges and allowed telemetry domains
- deployment-acceptance-checklist.pdf — tests we expect you to run during the rack-level smoke test
- manifests/ (kustomize overlays) and cert-rotation notes

Control-plane endpoints (FQDNs):
- control.redwood-inference.com (mTLS, port 443) — primary control plane
- ce-ctrl.us-west-1.redwood-inference.com (region attachment) — fallback path

Suggested firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to control.redwood-inference.com and ce-ctrl.us-west-1.redwood-inference.com; allow inbound from our health-check IP ranges listed in the CSV. We try to avoid static IP pinning where possible and instead publish short-lived SRV records and mTLS certs — the diagram shows the cert distribution flow.

Ephemeral egress notes:
- During model pulls we will open short-lived HTTPS connections to model-repo.redwood-inference.com (we recommend allowing egress to that FQDN).
- Telemetry and call-home: metrics.redwood-inference.com (443) — these are optional for the pilot; you can proxy them through a customer side collector.
- If you run strict NAT egress policies, the ephemeral-egress-policy.yaml includes a minimal CIDR set we use for outbound ephemeral flows.

I also attached the acceptance checklist PDF. Action items for your infra team:
1) Validate firewall rules against the CSV list
2) Confirm whether you want telemetry proxied or allowed directly
3) Confirm path MTU > 1400 for binary model pulls (we've seen issues with smaller MTUs)

If you want, Jonas and I can join a 30-min validation call on Tuesday to walk through the checklist.

Thanks —
Sooj
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- vpc_artifact_index.csv (text/csv)
- deployment-acceptance-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@acme-corp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lin Wu <lin.wu@brytecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data handoff: deployment artifact inventory & ephemeral routing plan

Jake / Soojin —

Quick operational notes from the control-plane side: 
- We will sign control-plane mTLS certs for the pilot; the CSR flow is in the manifests folder. Please ensure your CA acceptance script trusts our intermediate for the pilot window.
- Control plane health-checks expect liveness probes from the customer to come from a small set of source IPs (listed in the CSV). If you have an egress NAT gateway, please annotate the gateway with the external IPs before testing.
- For data-plane demarcation: runtime traffic (model inference) flows exclusively over private peering; we will not open inference traffic to the public Internet during the pilot. If you need to replicate logs to GCP/Azure buckets, we'll coordinate an ops-only temporary egress rule.

I've also attached an updated controlplane diagram (controlplane-diagram-v2.drawio.png) — it highlights the service-to-service auth path and the routing override we propose for the fallback region.

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: controlplane-diagram-v2.drawio.png (image/png)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Jake Porter <jake.porter@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control/Data handoff: deployment artifact inventory & ephemeral routing plan

Thanks for the artifacts — I reviewed the acceptance checklist. Two ask items before we mark the artifact set as final: 

1) Can we add a short "rollback play" paragraph in the checklist PDF describing how to gracefully flip traffic back to the staging control plane (we've pulled a template from our internal runbooks; I'll paste the suggested steps).
2) Please confirm any CRT rotation windows that will occur in the +7 days after cutover (we want to avoid automated rotations during our acceptance tests).

Soojin — if you can drop a 3-line rollback play into the checklist and confirm rotation windows, I think we can sign off and hand the materials to ACME's ops team.

Kimberly
Director, Deployment Ops, Redwood Inference

Lin will coordinate the crossconnect proof-of-connect and I'll follow up if NAT mapping gets in the way.

Jake
